messages:
olivia: Heads up — I sketched a proposal for schema enforcement + cardinality caps for runtime metrics. Want eng-runtime, eng-sre, and devex eyes before I open the PR. Short list: namespace metrics, whitelist labels, per-label cardinality caps, and a CI validator that fails on high-cardinality additions.

sam: +1 on a validator. can we make it opt-in for private deployments? some on-prem customers send app-level tags we can't control.

olivia: good call. proposal includes an allowlist override per-customer and a flag to opt out of enforcement in Private. default for Hosted/Dedicated is enforced.

lee: curious about the label naming convention — do we prefix all internal labels with `ri_`? suggests avoiding collisions with apps.

olivia: yes: `ri_*` for platform labels, `app_*` for customer-provided. example: `ri_route`, `ri_model`, `app_team`. keeps Prom/OTel queries predictable.

maya: cardinality caps? what numbers are we thinking? per-label vs combination cardinality?

olivia: proposing per-label caps: route=500, model=200, instance_id=50, env=10. combination cardinality (unique series) target is 1M per cluster. We also want sampling and prefix/KV caching to avoid high-cardinality spikes.

nate: route=500 seems high if we accept path params. we should normalize routes in runtime (strip ids) and only allow normalized routes into metrics. runtime-engine can do that.

olivia: yes runtime will normalize by default, and we want a lint rule in the SDK that flags dynamic segments. example normalizer: `/v1/users/{id}/profile` -> `/v1/users/:id/profile`.

infra-bot: CI check suggestion: `make telemetry-validate` which runs `telemetry-lint` to verify label whitelist and estimate cardinality from sample data. Fails on > threshold or new unknown labels.

sam: how will this affect dashboards? we need a migration plan: dashboards that used forbidden labels should get a mapping layer and alert to owners.

olivia: plan: preflight job to scan dashboards (Grafana/Looker) for deprecated labels, create tickets, and provide remap layer for 3 months. console UX will show a banner on affected dashboards with migration steps.

maya: rollouts UX: if we change a label name or cap, we need gradual enforcement. can we do canary validation that warns but doesn't fail for a week?

olivia: yes: stages = WARN_ONLY (1w), AUDIT (30d retention of incidents), ENFORCE. team owners get email + slack notifications during WARN_ONLY.

lee: OTel tracing: labels that get promoted to metrics need stable names. do we add a metadata registry for metric provenance?

olivia: adding a small metadata service with entries: metric_name, source_lib, ingestion_policy, owners. this will back the console's telemetry page.

nate: will the validator check history? if a new label increases cardinality on a metric that already exists, we should detect it before merging.

infra-bot: `telemetry-lint` supports a `--historical-scan` flag that checks last-30-day cardinality and simulates impact. adds a comment to PR with risk score.

olivia: next steps: I'll post the RFC doc and the validator repo link. asking for quick reviews by EOD Wednesday so we can alpha the CI hook next sprint. ping @eng-runtime @eng-sre @devex.

sam: will review. also add a checklist for private deployment onboarding so infra teams know how to toggle the allowlist override.

maya: thanks — also request a small dashboard in console showing "Top label cardinality by metric" so teams can proactively act.

olivia: noted. console owners: can you add a card to the roadmap? cc @devex-bot

devex-bot: added ticket RDW-telemetry-cardinality-dashboard to backlog (priority: P2).

olivia: thanks everyone. I'll push the PR with examples + `telemetry-lint` integration tomorrow.
